I had a very disappointing experience at the Prabhadevi (Century Bazaar) center during my sonography appointment.

My appointment was scheduled for 3:45 PM. While booking, I was informed that the doctor might be slightly delayed, so I arrived on time and followed the pre-test instructions, including drinking water. What was most frustrating was the lack of transparency from the front desk. Despite repeated inquiries, we were only told “the doctor will come soon,” without any clear update or explanation. This is especially difficult for patients who may already be physically or emotionally uncomfortable.

The experience worsened once the doctor, Dr. Roma Lala, arrived. Her behavior was extremely unprofessional. She was loudly scolding staff inside the sonography room, and her tone could be heard clearly outside, creating a very tense environment.

During my scan, there was no effort to communicate calmly or reassure me. When I asked about my results, the response was abrupt and unclear, which only increased my anxiety.

While Metropolis as a brand has a strong reputation, this particular experience was far below expectations. I would strongly suggest better time management, clearer communication, and more empathetic patient handling, especially in diagnostic settings.

Recommendation: If you are planning to visit this centre, I would strongly advise avoiding it for sonography services.

HbA1c Test: Purpose, Procedure, Normal Range & Results
May 26, 2026 - By Lupin Diagnostics
India has over 10.1 crore people living with diabetes. A daily finger-prick reading captures just one moment. The HbA1c test normal range tells a fuller story. This simple blood test reveals your average blood sugar over three months. Here is everything you need to know about it.
What Is the HbA1c Test and How Does It Work?
Glucose in your blood naturally sticks to haemoglobin, the protein inside red blood cells. The more sugar in your blood, the more gets attached. Since red blood cells live for roughly three months, the HbA1c test captures your average blood sugar level over that entire period.
This makes it far more reliable than a single fasting reading. A fasting test changes with your last meal or stress levels. Glycated haemoglobin, on the other hand, reflects steady patterns. Think of it as a three-month report card for your blood sugar.
Here is how it differs from routine glucose checks:
A fasting blood sugar test measures glucose at one point in time.
The HbA1c test shows a percentage reflecting 90-day glucose control.
It does not swing based on a recent meal or exercise session.
